;Armed conflicts and attacks 
*Security forces block roads leading to [[intelligence service|intelligence]] buildings in [[Sudan]] as gunfire is heard in the capital [[Khartoum]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-security/gunfire-heard-in-sudanese-capital-witness-idUSKBN1ZD19F (Reuters)]
*[[Battle of Chinagodrar]]
**[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] claims responsibility for the attack in Chinagodrar, [[Tillabéri Region]], [[Niger]], that killed at least 89 [[Niger Armed Forces|Nigerien soldiers]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-niger-security/islamic-state-claims-responsibility-for-niger-army-base-attack-idUSKBN1ZD1ZZ (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*The [[United Kingdom]] bans the use of [[credit card]]s to make bets both for [[Online gambling|online]] and offline [[gambling in the United Kingdom|gambling]], including the purchase of [[lottery]] tickets. The only exception to the ban is the purchase of lottery tickets in face-to-face transactions. The [[Gambling Commission]] says the ban will come into effect on April 14. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-britain-gambling/britain-bans-using-credit-cards-to-gamble-idUKKBN1ZD0PF (Reuters)]
*In [[India]], [[economy of India|economic]] slowdown has adversely impacted employment generation in the country, as nearly 1,600,000 fewer jobs are projected to be created in FY20 compared to 8,970,000 fresh jobs in FY19. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/indicators/slowdown-may-hurt-job-creation-sbi/articleshow/73239579.cms (''The Economic Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 57 people are killed and others are missing after [[avalanche]]s in [[Pakistan]]-controlled [[Kashmir]] over the last 24 hours, senior [[government of Pakistan|government]] officials say. In [[India]]n-administered Kashmir, at least 10 are killed. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-disaster/at-least-67-killed-by-avalanches-in-pakistan-india-government-officials-idUSKBN1ZD0TU (Reuters)]
*[[Chemical Industries of Ethylene Oxide explosion]]
**An explosion at a [[chemical plant]] in [[Tarragona]], [[Catalonia]], [[Spain]], kills two members of staff and another man 3&nbsp;km away. Seven other people are injured. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51113132 (BBC News)]
*[[Delta Air Lines Flight 89]]
**At least 44 people, including twenty elementary school children, are injured after [[Delta Air Lines|Delta]]  Flight 89, bound  for [[Shanghai]], dumped jet fuel over [[Los Angeles]] before making an emergency landing at [[Los Angeles International Airport]]. None of the reported injuries required hospitalization. [https://time.com/5764959/jet-fuel-playground-children-los-angeles/ (''Time'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2020/01/15/delta-dumps-fuel-expert-defends-pilots/4476137002/ (''USA Today'')]

;International relations
*[[Foreign relations of Tonga]]
**[[Tonga]] pays an outstanding fee in order not to lose its voting rights at the [[United Nations General Assembly]]. Tonga was among seven countries suspended last week for not paying their assessed contributions. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/407297/tonga-pays-outstanding-un-fees-govt (Radio New Zealand)]
*[[Libyan peace process]]
**General [[Khalifa Haftar]], head of the [[Libyan National Army]] (LNA), refuses to sign a [[ceasefire]] agreement after talks in [[Moscow]] brokered by [[Russia]] and [[Turkey]] yesterday with [[Government of National Accord]] leader [[Fayez al-Sarraj]]. He says that the deal "ignores many of the Libyan army's demands". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/libya-haftar-leaves-moscow-signing-ceasefire-agreement-200114064637135.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Indonesia–Thailand relations]]
**[[Thailand|Thai]] Army Chief [[Apirat Kongsompong]] and his [[Indonesia]]n counterpart [[Andika Perkasa]] sign an intelligence-sharing agreement aimed at combating the [[South Thailand insurgency|insurgency in Thailand’s southern provinces]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/thailand--indonesia-to-share-intelligence-to-combat-insurgents-12262750 (CNA)]

;Law and crime
*After the conviction of [[serial rapist]] [[Reynhard Sinaga]], [[Mohammad Idris]], the mayor of [[Depok]], [[West Java]], [[Indonesia]], says he plans to raid the local [[LGBT rights in Indonesia|LGBT]] community and is condemned by [[human rights]] [[activist]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-indonesia-lgbt/indonesia-rights-body-condemns-lgbt-raids-ordered-by-mayor-after-uk-rape-case-idUSKBN1ZD0J6?il=0 (Reuters)]
*American rapper [[Jay-Z]] and his philanthropic organization Team Roc file a federal lawsuit against [[Mississippi Department of Corrections]] commissioner Pelicia E. Hall and [[Mississippi State Penitentiary]] superintendent Marshal Turner over the abusive and neglectful treatment of their prisoners, which they claim has led to the deaths of at least three people. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/jay-z-goes-bat-mississippi-prisoners-files-federal-lawsuit-n1115616 (NBC News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-51126128 (BBC News)]

;Politics and Elections
*[[Politics of Guatemala]]
**[[Alejandro Giammattei]] takes the oath of office as [[President of Guatemala]] for the next four years. Also 160 new [[Congress of Guatemala|members of Congress]] are installed for a new parliamentary period of four years. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-guatemala-politics-president/giammattei-sworn-in-as-guatemalan-president-after-delays-idUSKBN1ZE044 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of South Korea]]
**The [[National Assembly (South Korea)|National Assembly]] of South Korea elects and sworns in [[Chung Sye-kyun]] as [[Prime Minister of South Korea|Prime Minister]], succeeding [[Lee Nak-yeon]]. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200113009151320 (Yonhap News Agency)]
;Science and technology 
*[[Microsoft]] officially ends support for the [[Windows 7]] [[operating system]]. Microsoft says its Windows 7 users can still use their computers, but warns they will be at "greater risk for [[computer virus|viruses]] and [[malware]]". [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/01/13/tech/microsoft-windows-7-support/index.html (CNN Business)]
